failing.summary: commands/prepare-this-repo.md:193-202: Step 5 tells the agent to run `abcd ahoy install` then `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` unconditionally, and says 'a committed hook is not a running hook until git is pointed at it'. Since 0.13.3 banlist health reads the global/system hooks path (CHANGELOG iss-2610020704152920) and reports it as `foreign`; the binary's own fix hint for that state says 'never override it with a local hooks path, which would shadow it in this clone' (internal/core/ahoy/banlist_scaffold.go:794-797), and commands/ahoy.md:79-81 says the same. Following step 5 verbatim in a clone under a global dispatcher shadows that dispatcher for the clone. Judged not to make a user act wrongly in the release-gate sense: it applies only when a global or system core.hooksPath is in force, the `hooks_path: foreign` report from the same install run contradicts it on the spot, and it is reversed with `git config --unset core.hooksPath`. Fix: condition the second command on `hooks_path` reading `unarmed`.
failing.note: Misleads no action (the binary's own refusal text supplies what the page lacks); corrected in the post-cut follow-up change, since correcting it now would change the content commit and re-run every review.
